subject: ventures/automatic-driveway-gate-bid-calculator
auditor: agent session (Claude), independent quality auditor subagent, see run record
professional: an automatic gate installer/estimator at a fence and gate contractor who bids swing and slide operator installs; they check first that the operator is sized to the leaf weight and length, that labor hours and trench/conduit scale with the job, that every entrapment zone has the UL 325 (2016+) monitored external protection (photo eyes and/or edges) and the gate meets ASTM F2200, that permits are a line, that margin is not confused with markup, and that the rate card is sourced

evidence.correctness: Arithmetic is exact: a scratch script (recompute.mjs, imports calc.mjs) and hand work reproduce all four presets and every figure on the two marketing pages to the cent (12 ft single: 12.95 h, material $3,035, cost $4,684.02, price $6,505.58; 16 ft dual masonry: 42.89 h, $10,024, $14,716.71, $20,439.88; 18 ft slide $10,143.97 / 22.75 h; 14 ft wood $9,808.81; compareStyles 16 ft steel masonry single $15,395 / slide $16,741 / dual $20,440; 12 ft existing slide $7,585 / dual $9,165). Margin math is right: (price-cost)/price = 28.0000% (markup 38.89%). Held to 2 because outputs a user would act on are wrong for real jobs: leafHeightFt is validated and printed on the proposal but changes nothing (height 5 vs 10 ft both $6,505.58, also in the browser on the dual preset), a slide gate's leaf is priced at the opening width with no cantilever tail, and one fixed photo-eye kit is priced whatever the style or number of entrapment zones.
evidence.completeness: README features checked in Chromium via Playwright (walk.cjs against a local static server): presets load (dual preset price $20,439.88, '2 operators · 3 new columns'), three-style comparison renders and sorts, proposed-price verdict ('At $4,500.00 this job loses $10,216.71 ... walk-away $14,716.71'), blank width shows 'Opening width must be greater than zero', proposal prints with scope lines, deposit split, held-until date and signature block and leaks no cost/wage figures, no horizontal scroll at 375 px, no console errors. Stated limitations (intercom, mag lock, traffic control not modelled) are honest. llms.txt hosts are github.io in source but the deploy rewrites them (source-only, not counted).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 142 tests, 142 pass. Seven seeded mutants via quality_mutate.py: margin-to-markup, dual column count, photo-eye made optional, weight factor dropped from hang hours, break-even threshold, margin >=100 guard all caught; dropping columnMaterial from extraCost (the figure behind the 'almost half is extra work' claim and the extra-share bar) survived. No test asserts that leaf height affects anything, which is how the dead input shipped.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (527 lines), index.html calc wiring and proposal block, vs pages. Pure DOM-free engine, explicit number() validation, a strict yes/no flag parser that refuses unknown words, presets frozen, compareStyles documented as using suggested kits. Defects: leafHeightFt is parsed and returned but unused (calc.mjs:266); trench is a flat 3 h / $185 regardless of run length; share/proposal modules are generated and shared across ventures, which is fine.
evidence.claims: Checked: Jobber page (founded 2011, Edmonton, home-service FSM, subscription, no invented price, non-affiliation) - consistent with public record, pass. $4,500 page: every figure ($4,684.02, -$184.02, $14,716.71, -$10,216.71, $347.49/h = 4500/12.95, $104.92/h = 4500/42.89, '70% cut' = 69.8%) recomputed, pass, and it is labelled as the tool's own defaults. Fails/partials: 'Almost half of that dual bid is extra work' is 45.4% of cost but 32.7% of the bid price; 'a published $4,500 automatic-gate special' and '$350 a foot' are uncited; how-much page says 'a slide is one operator and a track' and 'the track and the receiver posts are their own hours' but there is no track/roller line in calc.mjs; the FAQ says whether an install meets the safety standard 'is a judgment call for whoever pulls the permit', which misstates UL 325 (a listing and installation requirement, not discretion). The $4,500 page's 'still lose money on each one' rests entirely on uncited ballpark rates. Disclaimers present on every page.
evidence.fitness: Walked a 16 ft dual steel masonry job with a $4,500 considered price to a printed proposal in Chromium: it works and the customer copy is clean. But an estimator hits in the first hour: no operator class/duty check against leaf weight and length (a 40 ft x 8 ft steel slide gets the same $1,850 single operator), no trench length or electrician line, one photo-eye kit for every style, and the proposal prints at the below-cost $4,500 with no warning on the proposal itself (the warning is only in the calculator verdict).
evidence.domain: Compared against UL 325 (2016+ requirement for monitored external entrapment protection on each entrapment zone, open and close directions for slide and swing), ASTM F2200 (gate construction, cantilever slide gate geometry), and common trade practice (cantilever slide leaf ~ opening x 1.5; operator chosen by gate weight/length/duty cycle; AC trench priced by the foot from the source). Margin-on-price method is correct, permit is a line, weight factor on leaf/hours is sensible. Departures: no operator sizing, single photo-eye kit regardless of zones, slide leaf length = opening, trench not by distance, leaf height ignored. Rate card is self-described 'ballpark shop figures, not a catalog' with no source.

defects.what: Leaf height is a required, validated input and is printed on the proposal ('16 ft opening x 6 ft leaf') but has no effect on leaf cost, hang hours or operator: a 10 ft leaf prices the same as a 5 ft one.

No operator sizing against leaf weight/length: every style gets one fixed-price operator per leaf whatever the gate (a 40 ft x 8 ft steel slide gets the same $1,850 operator as an 18 ft aluminum one).

One fixed photo-eye kit is added regardless of style or entrapment zones; UL 325 (2016+) requires monitored external entrapment protection for each zone, and the proposal states '2 gate operators with safety photo-eyes' on a dual swing priced with one kit.

Slide gate leaf length is the opening width; a cantilever slide leaf typically runs about 1.5x the opening (counterbalance tail), so slide leaf dollars and hours are understated, and no track/roller line exists despite the page saying the track is its own hours.
AC power is a flat 3 h and $185 trench/conduit with no run length and no electrician line, the item that varies most between gate jobs.
'Almost half of that dual bid is columns, loops, power, and access' - the figure is 45.4% of cost, 32.7% of the bid price; and the extraCost composition is untested (seeded mutant survived).
FAQ says whether an install meets the safety standard 'is a judgment call for whoever pulls the permit', which misstates UL 325/ASTM F2200 as discretionary.

Rate card (operator $1,350-1,850, leaf $85-95/lf, masonry $950/column, photo eyes $165) and the 'published $4,500 special' / '$350 a foot' framing are uncited; the $4,500 page's 'lose money on each one' rests on them.
The customer proposal prints at a considered price below total cost with no warning on the proposal step (verdict only).

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 3, median 2); finished (completeness 3). The arithmetic is exact: four presets and every number on the how-much and $4,500 pages recompute to the cent, margin is correctly on price, and 142 tests catch 6 of 7 seeded mutants. The gap is the gate itself: leaf height is collected and printed on the proposal but ignored, there is no operator sizing by weight or length, one photo-eye kit covers every style despite UL 325's per-zone requirement, slide leaves are priced at the opening width with no cantilever tail or track, and the AC trench is a flat line. Marketing pages are honest about using the tool's own defaults and the Jobber page invents nothing, but 'almost half the bid' is 33% of price and the rate card is uncited.
